signals.title: Out There
signals.description: * Reminder: The Savor of the Month theme for October is WATER. Details here ; Supporters can share their findings in the thread here . Check it out! “Writing in the places that shape and sustain us.” Fall (or at least post-summer) finally seems to be arriving here in New Orleans. And it is almost time — wherever you are — for Write Out . This is an annual undertaking of the National Writing Project , developed in conjunction with the National Park Service . As I wrote last year : The core idea is pretty simple: get outside, and write. Write about your environment, write to your environment, observe and attend to nature, use the craft of writing to sharpen your senses, and use your senses to sharpen your writing. “The goal is to be inspired by the world around us ,” the NWP writes, “and to connect and learn through place-based writing and sharing.” Nothing (well, maybe apart from the actual weather) is stopping you from writing outside any time. But Write Out is a kick in the pants, a kind of open-to-anyone annual two-week event, which the NWP promotes through various prompts and other resources aimed at educators but available to all. This year Write Out happens October 11–25, with the lovely theme Write Where We Stand — “writing in the places that shape and sustain us.” Every year NWP publishes a “ choice board ” of theme-related prompts; here are a few (condensed and slightly modified versions) of my favorites for this year. (Click through on each prompt title for the full NWP context/instructions.) Poetically Advocate A Place You Love . Take inspiration from Don Welch’s poem “ Advice From a Provincial ,“ and identify three “outdoor images or phenomena that are wondrous about your place. Use them to create a poetic letter to someone who doesn’t really know” the place you love, or at least not like you know it. Link Words and Image s. Snap some pictures around your community. Take your time. Choose one that captures something to celebrate — and one that captures something you would like to change. Pair these images. “ What story do they tell when you look at them together? Give your story a title, caption your images, and share your work.” Speak Like A River. Poets Amanda Eke and Mario José Pagán Morales consider the Bronx River, and what stories it might tell. In a place you know, reflect on “ what that place has witnessed , remembered, celebrated, protected, or survived. … If this river, tree, park, or wooded pathway could talk — tell us poems, tell us stories — what do you think it would say?” Write about it. Leave a comment THERE’S MORE! In connection with Write Out, there are two online events that sound cool: Hawaiian Kilo: Writing Rooted in Place Native Hawaiians developed a practice known as Kilo — “to watch, observe, examine, or forecast.” This means closely observing the natural world and its patterns, ideally to better steward the environment. A Zoom workshop, “led by teachers from the Waiākea Intermediate School in Hilo Hawai'i,” happens October 13, 2026, 6 pm US Central time . Details and (free) registration here . Haiku + Comic = Haikomic The Write Time with Write Out Ambassador Grant Snider on October 20 . Snider is a writer/artist who combines haiku with comics. (Details on that here , and at his newsletter. ) And he is this year’s Write Out Author Ambassador. Check the Write Out newsletter for event details as they emerge. I really like the sound of this and hope to revisit. Grant Snider, via Incidental Comics Leave a comment PS I was a Write Out Ambassador last year. I love Write Out! BECOME A SUPPORTER Do you believe in this newsletter’s mission — to help us all stay human and engaged and creative in a world of (mis)information overload and AI distraction? Then you should join the community of TAoN Supporters! You’ll get access to the full archives as well as Supporter-only bonus posts and threads. Your support makes this newsletter possible. Seriously. Thank you! Subscribe now THE NEXT FREE EDITION IN TWO WEEKS! IN OTHER NEWS David Lee Roth , EMT . “ Reading Maps plots the routes characters travel in novels and films — you can trace the Pequod’s ocean path as it chases Moby Dick, or Victor Frankenstein’s pursuit of his monster from Geneva to the Arctic.” — Recomendo Lighthouses of the World , a digital map. Via Popular Science . “What Gertrude Stein, T. S. Eliot and Joan Didion Really Meant With Their Most Famous Aphorisms .” The International Dada Archive collects scanned Dada pamphlets from the early 20th century. Mark Frauenfelder found one in English called The Blind Man , co-edited by Marcel Duchamp. Its second issue, from 1917, covered the controversy around Duchamp’s Fountain , a urinal he submitted under the name Richard Mutt to the Society of Independent Artists exhibition. More from Mark here . Shadows . Via Street Art Utopia. Tobie Tse “combines hand-stitched textiles, illustration and digital motion to create visual responses to music.” Tom Waits spoken word piece : OKAY THAT’S IT! As always, I value your feedback (suggestions, critiques, positive reinforcement, constructive insults directed at me, not at anyone else , etc.), as well as your tips or stories or personal noticing rituals, things we need a word for, and of course your icebreakers : consumed@robwalker.net. Or use the comments. —> Or just click the heart symbol. That always makes my day. signals.title: AI Design Conference 2027 tickets are live: Learn the AI workflows top designers use
signals.description: Hey Design System Friend 👋 We are back! Our AI Design Systems Conference returns on March 10 and 11 2027 and tickets are live right now . Get two days of live sessions on agentic design systems, Claude Code, Cursor, MCPs, CLIs and AI workflows with the designers who build them at Anthropic, OpenAI and Netflix . 👀 Last year’s edition was so popular that we sold out and had to close ticket sales before the conference even started. This time there are 1,000 spots and they are only available while they last. 👉 Get your ticket for $499 🎤 First speakers for 2027 The first five speakers build these workflows every day at Anthropic, OpenAI, Atlassian, Netflix and Yahoo: Frank Bach : Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic Katie Langerman : Design Systems at OpenAI Lewis Healey : Principal Design Technologist, Core Design at Atlassian Diana Wolosin : Senior AI Systems Architect, Ads at Netflix Brian Alfaro : Principal Designer, Design Systems at Yahoo More speakers will be announced soon 📅 First sessions announced Leaving the old tools behind: Building agentic design systems without Figma Michael Schultz (Managing Partner at Inverse) and Noga Enbar (Senior Product Designer at Inverse) How to get started with local LLMs as a designer: setup and real use cases Dirk Bahrenburg (Design System Architect and Founder at Bahrenburg Design Systems) How to build a CLI for your Design System Aimee Maroney (Design Engineer at Deva Studios) and Hannah Clarke (Design System Architect at Deva Studios) Watch all sessions live or in the recordings with lifetime access and keep the templates, files and prompts the speakers share. 🧠 What you will learn Agentic Design Systems, MCPs, CLIs, Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Skills, Subagents, Local LLMs, Design Tokens, Component Specs and Prompts. 🎟️ What your ticket includes 📺 Live conference on both days with Q&A after each talk 🤝 Networking board where attendees swap notes, prompts and workflows 📁 Templates, files and prompts shared by the speakers 📼 All conference recordings with lifetime access 🏆 Certificate of attendance for your CV and LinkedIn 👥 Bring your team Get 3 seats for $1,497 or 5 seats for $2,495. Every seat stays at $499 if you book before the price goes up on October 20. 💬 What attendees said about 2026 “As I have been telling EVERYONE I know, the best professional upskilling investment I have done in ages.” Sam Sabour , Senior Product Designer “Genuinely changed the direction of my career. How to use AI to streamline design system workflows, how MCPs work and how they connect design to code in ways I hadn’t imagined.” Elleta McDaniel , Design Systems Designer at CTRL_ALT_DESIGN Into Design Systems won Best Event and Community Champion at the Design System Awards 2025 by zeroheight. ⏳ Don’t wait The launch price ends on October 20 and there are only 1,000 spots in total. 👉 Save one of 1,000 spots Can’t wait to learn the newest AI workflows with you 👋 Sil

visualFeast.title: Step by step: How to find Design System + AI jobs faster with Claude Code and MCP
visualFeast.description: I gave our Design System job board an MCP server. Your AI agent can read the whole job board now. (What is an MCP? MCP is the standard that lets an agent call a tool instead of scraping a web page) Into Design Systems + AI is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Why? Good roles go early. By the time you have scrolled the job board and opened twelve tabs and read the postings properly the pile on the recruiter’s desk is deep. There are 225 open Design System roles on the board right now. Every one of them is checked by hand and closed postings drop out. Nobody reads 225 postings. You read four and apply to two. Your agent works through all of them. It runs at https://jobs.intodesignsystems.com/mcp It needs no key and no account and it can only read Below are the 30 prompts I run against it The last ones hand the whole job over to a cron job that checks the board every morning for you What is inside One line to connect the server. Everything after it is a prompt. 23 prompts for finding roles and reading salary bands and closing skill gaps and preparing for the interview. 7 prompts that hand the search to a cron job so your Mac checks the board while you sleep. The five tools and what each one answers. Step 1: connect it One line in your terminal (1 min) Paste this in Claude Code: claude mcp add -s user --transport http ids-jobs https://jobs.intodesignsystems.com/mcp The -s user part registers it for every folder. Leave it out and the server only exists in the folder you happened to be in. Then restart Claude Code once because tools load when a session starts. Quit it with /exit and start it again and ask “which tools do you have from ids-jobs?” No terminal at all? Claude Desktop and claude.ai do it in the interface: Settings then Connectors then Add custom connector. Paste the URL and start a new chat. Cursor and every other MCP client work too. The setup page has the config for each of them. Step 2: the prompts Put your CV in the folder you start Claude Code in or simply describe your skills. Then use these. Every number under a prompt is what the board answered on 21 August 2026. I want the roles that are worth my time Five prompts that cut 225 postings down to the handful you would actually take. 1. “Which Design System roles were posted in the last two weeks? Optional: Which of them fit my CV?” The one I use most. 57 roles came in over the last fourteen days. Here are the five newest: Malt Head of Experience Systems & AI France / Germany 21 Aug ICEYE Staff/Lead Product Designer, Design System Finland 21 Aug eBay Principal Designer - Design Systems USA 21 Aug Figma Product Designer, AI Models USA remote 21 Aug Harvey Product Designer, Design Systems USA 21 Aug Your agent then keeps the ones that match your CV and tells you what you are missing per role. It reads the requirements the company wrote and not the job title. 2. “Only the remote ones that ask for AI skills please” Across the whole board 32 roles are remote and name AI or agentic skills in the posting. Those are the ones I would read first. 3. “Compare the Netflix and the General Motors role for me. Which one is closer to what I have done?” Two postings side by side with your CV as the yardstick. 4. “Put the eight best matches in a table with company and title and link and one line on why it fits. Save it as shortlist.md” Now you have one working file instead of twelve open tabs. Tell it to strike the row once you have applied. 5. “Go through shortlist.md and tell me which of these roles are still open” Closed postings drop off the board so this is a real check and not a guess. Run it before you spend an evening on an application for a role that filled two weeks ago. I want a number for the salary talk Three prompts so you name a figure that came from postings and not from a feeling. 6. “What do postings pay for a Staff level Design System role?” 46 postings state a range themselves. The median sits between 162,600 and 220,000 USD and the highest range on the board tops out at 710,000. Almost all of those postings are US roles because pay transparency laws require the number there so do not carry them into another country. 7. “Which US roles ask for design tokens and what do they pay?” 17 US postings name design tokens. Eleven of them state a range and four of those top out above 200,000 USD. The highest is the Netflix Systems Designer role in Design Foundations at 260,000 to 400,000. 8. “This posting states no salary. What do comparable roles on the board pay?” You get the range from the postings that do state one plus which level and country they came from. That is a reference point and not their budget. Say the number first anyway. I want to know what to learn next Four prompts for the months when you are not applying and want to be ready when you are. 9. “Which skills come up in most postings that my CV does not mention?” Run this when you are not applying yet. It tells you what to learn next instead of guessing. 93 of the 135 postings we hold the full text for ask for AI or agentic skills. 10. “Read the Netflix posting. Which requirements do I not have yet and where do I learn them?” The server does not stop at the gap. find_learning takes the missing skill and helps you find where to learn it. It names the recorded conference session from the Into Design Systems AI Conference that covers it. Ask about MCP and you get Diana Wolosin , Netflix (ex Indeed) on machine-readable design systems for MCP and LLMs. Ask about agentic design systems and you get Romina Kavcic on the five agentic flows. 11. “Which roles do not ask for AI skills at all?” 48 of the described postings ask for none. Useful if you are still building that muscle and want something you can start on Monday. 12. “Which words do these postings use for the work I already do?” Vocabulary research and nothing else. You still write your own CV but you write it in the words the market uses. I want to walk into the interview prepared Four prompts that turn their own posting into your prep sheet. 13. “Read this posting and tell me the three things they care about most and what I should have ready as evidence” My prep prompt. You get their own wording back plus the questions worth preparing for. 14. “What does this posting not ask for?” Stops you preparing three days for a topic nobody will bring up. 15. “Give me three questions to ask them at the end. Base them on their own posting” Questions that come out of their requirements land differently than the ones everybody asks. 16. “Which companies have more than three roles open?” General Motors has 5 and Netflix has 4. Coinbase and ESET and Yassir have 3 each. Several roles open at once usually means a team is being built. Worth a direct message. I want to know where the roles are Four prompts before you plan a move or a timezone or a year of applications. 17. “Where do most Design System roles sit right now?” USA has 119 and the United Kingdom 16 and Germany 14. Canada and France have 12 each. Useful if you are weighing a move or a timezone. 18. “How many of the German roles can be done remotely?” One of the 14. Ask that before you spend a year applying from a country you do not want to move to. 19. “How concentrated is the board? How many companies are hiring and how many have more than one role?” 190 companies are hiring right now and 27 of them have two or more roles open. 20. “Are there contract roles?” Seven right now. get_job carries the employment type so you can sort permanent from contract before you read anything. I am the one hiring Three prompts for the other side of the table. 21. “Compare our job description against the open Design System postings and tell me what other companies name that we leave out” You get back what the other postings name and your description leaves out. 22. “What do other companies call this role?” 88 of the open postings carry Design System Designer in the title and 94 carry Product Designer and 23 carry Design System Engineer. 98 say Staff or Senior. Name the role the way the people you want are searching. 23. “Who are we competing with for these people right now?” Every company with an open role in your corner of the board plus how many they have open. That is your candidate’s other tab. Step 3: let it check the board every morning A cron job is your Mac running something on a schedule without you. You never have to write one. You describe what should happen and when and Claude Code sets it up. The daily check Save your CV as cv.md in a folder. Mine is ~/jobs . Start Claude Code in that folder and paste this. 24. “Set up a job check that runs every weekday at 8 in the morning. Read cv.md in this folder. Ask the ids-jobs server for the roles posted in the last seven days that can be done remotely and keep the ones that fit my CV. Write them into today.md with one line per role: company and title and why it fits. If nothing fits write nothing new. It has to run on its own without asking me anything because I am not at the machine at 8. Put it in my crontab and run it once now so I can see that it works.” Claude writes the script and sets the schedule and shows you the first result. Here is what came back for me: SAP Senior UX Designer - Design Systems Microsoft Principal Product Designer, Design Systems Netflix Systems Designer, Design Foundations Clio Staff Product Designer, Design Systems Babylist Staff Product Designer, AI Builder Two things to know before you run it. The one click you have to give: Claude asks before it edits your crontab. Say yes and it is done. Full Disk Access: on macOS your terminal needs it under System Settings then Privacy and Security. Without it the 8 o’clock run cannot read your CV. Four more worth scheduling The daily check is one job. These four run next to it. 25. “Same thing but once a week. Monday at 9. Everything from the last seven days grouped by country and put the remote ones first” The daily one is for an active search. This is the version you keep running when you are not looking. It takes two minutes to read on Monday. 26. “Watch Figma and Netflix and Atlassian for me. Check every morning and only write something into watch.md when one of them posts a new Design System role” For the three companies you would leave for. Silence most days is the point. 27. “On the first of every month ask for the hiring numbers and append them to market.md with the date. Open roles and remote share and AI share and the salary range” After four months you have your own trend line. The board only tells you today and the file tells you the direction. 28. “Send the result to name@example.com instead of writing a file” Add that sentence to any of the prompts above and it lands in your inbox. Checking and stopping it You never open crontab yourself. You ask. 29. “Show me what you scheduled and when it runs next” 30. “Stop the daily job check but leave the Monday one running” You never touch crontab yourself. You say what you want and Claude edits it. What it does not do It does not apply for you: every role links to the employer’s own page and the server never sends anything on your behalf. It should not write your cover letter: a letter that came out of a model reads like one. Use this to work out what the role wants and then write it yourself. It only knows Design System and AI design roles: nothing else is on the board. Try it claude mcp add -s user --transport http ids-jobs https://jobs.intodesignsystems.com/mcp Setup page with all clients: jobs.intodesignsystems.com/mcp-guide . The board itself lives at jobs.intodesignsystems.com . A longer version of this walkthrough lives on our blog. It adds what to put in cv.md so the matching actually works plus a troubleshooting table for the things that go wrong: read it on intodesignsystems.com . Good luck! You got this! If you get stuck or you have an idea for a tool the server should have then write me on LinkedIn . Sil Bormüller Founder @ Into Design Systems P.S. Missing the AI skills these roles ask for? Level up. The Into Design Systems AI conference has hands-on talks on AI workflows and Claude Code and Cursor and Design System automation from industry experts. Back in August, I tried a little experiment: publishing a question from my ongoing Icebreaker series as a stand-alone post, rather than a secondary item in the main newsletter. The hope was that this would encourage readers to actually answer in the comments. And it did! So I’m doing it again. All are welcome to chime in. Noticing is about other people, too. The Icebreaker series aims to help with that. There’s a central collection spot for all the icebreakers to date, here . Today’s icebreaker comes from me. What is the most recent, or most personally important, book that you’ve read twice (or more)? I would probably stipulate no children’s books; I think that’s a different discussion. But otherwise I’d be open to just seeing where the question leads — I think it’s somehow more interesting than just asking for someone’s “favorite” book. This subject of re-reading books has popped up randomly a couple of times for me lately, and made me think about how long it’s been since I’ve done it. I guess I now worry that I just don’t have enough time to repeat a book when there are so many I haven’t read once! That said, the most recent was The Ladies’ Paradise , by Zola, which I read for a second time about 10 years ago. The book I’ve read the most times is Native Son , three times (all in my 20s, I believe). What about you? Love to hear your thoughts! Leave a comment And please send your favorite icebreaker (whether you made it up or found it elsewhere) to consumed@robwalker.net . Previously: OKAY THAT’S IT! As always, I value your feedback (suggestions, critiques, positive reinforcement, constructive insults directed at me, not at anyone else , etc.), as well as your tips or stories or personal noticing rituals, things we need a word for, and of course your icebreakers : consumed@robwalker.net. Or use the comments. —> Or just click the heart symbol. That always makes my day. graphicDesign.title: Step by step: How to find Design System + AI jobs faster with Claude Code and MCP
graphicDesign.description: I gave our Design System job board an MCP server. Your AI agent can read the whole job board now. (What is an MCP? MCP is the standard that lets an agent call a tool instead of scraping a web page) Into Design Systems + AI is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Why? Good roles go early. By the time you have scrolled the job board and opened twelve tabs and read the postings properly the pile on the recruiter’s desk is deep. There are 225 open Design System roles on the board right now. Every one of them is checked by hand and closed postings drop out. Nobody reads 225 postings. You read four and apply to two. Your agent works through all of them. It runs at https://jobs.intodesignsystems.com/mcp It needs no key and no account and it can only read Below are the 30 prompts I run against it The last ones hand the whole job over to a cron job that checks the board every morning for you What is inside One line to connect the server. Everything after it is a prompt. 23 prompts for finding roles and reading salary bands and closing skill gaps and preparing for the interview. 7 prompts that hand the search to a cron job so your Mac checks the board while you sleep. The five tools and what each one answers. Step 1: connect it One line in your terminal (1 min) Paste this in Claude Code: claude mcp add -s user --transport http ids-jobs https://jobs.intodesignsystems.com/mcp The -s user part registers it for every folder. Leave it out and the server only exists in the folder you happened to be in. Then restart Claude Code once because tools load when a session starts. Quit it with /exit and start it again and ask “which tools do you have from ids-jobs?” No terminal at all? Claude Desktop and claude.ai do it in the interface: Settings then Connectors then Add custom connector. Paste the URL and start a new chat. Cursor and every other MCP client work too. The setup page has the config for each of them. Step 2: the prompts Put your CV in the folder you start Claude Code in or simply describe your skills. Then use these. Every number under a prompt is what the board answered on 21 August 2026. I want the roles that are worth my time Five prompts that cut 225 postings down to the handful you would actually take. 1. “Which Design System roles were posted in the last two weeks? Optional: Which of them fit my CV?” The one I use most. 57 roles came in over the last fourteen days. Here are the five newest: Malt Head of Experience Systems & AI France / Germany 21 Aug ICEYE Staff/Lead Product Designer, Design System Finland 21 Aug eBay Principal Designer - Design Systems USA 21 Aug Figma Product Designer, AI Models USA remote 21 Aug Harvey Product Designer, Design Systems USA 21 Aug Your agent then keeps the ones that match your CV and tells you what you are missing per role. It reads the requirements the company wrote and not the job title. 2. “Only the remote ones that ask for AI skills please” Across the whole board 32 roles are remote and name AI or agentic skills in the posting. Those are the ones I would read first. 3. “Compare the Netflix and the General Motors role for me. Which one is closer to what I have done?” Two postings side by side with your CV as the yardstick. 4. “Put the eight best matches in a table with company and title and link and one line on why it fits. Save it as shortlist.md” Now you have one working file instead of twelve open tabs. Tell it to strike the row once you have applied. 5. “Go through shortlist.md and tell me which of these roles are still open” Closed postings drop off the board so this is a real check and not a guess. Run it before you spend an evening on an application for a role that filled two weeks ago. I want a number for the salary talk Three prompts so you name a figure that came from postings and not from a feeling. 6. “What do postings pay for a Staff level Design System role?” 46 postings state a range themselves. The median sits between 162,600 and 220,000 USD and the highest range on the board tops out at 710,000. Almost all of those postings are US roles because pay transparency laws require the number there so do not carry them into another country. 7. “Which US roles ask for design tokens and what do they pay?” 17 US postings name design tokens. Eleven of them state a range and four of those top out above 200,000 USD. The highest is the Netflix Systems Designer role in Design Foundations at 260,000 to 400,000. 8. “This posting states no salary. What do comparable roles on the board pay?” You get the range from the postings that do state one plus which level and country they came from. That is a reference point and not their budget. Say the number first anyway. I want to know what to learn next Four prompts for the months when you are not applying and want to be ready when you are. 9. “Which skills come up in most postings that my CV does not mention?” Run this when you are not applying yet. It tells you what to learn next instead of guessing. 93 of the 135 postings we hold the full text for ask for AI or agentic skills. 10. “Read the Netflix posting. Which requirements do I not have yet and where do I learn them?” The server does not stop at the gap. find_learning takes the missing skill and helps you find where to learn it. It names the recorded conference session from the Into Design Systems AI Conference that covers it. Ask about MCP and you get Diana Wolosin , Netflix (ex Indeed) on machine-readable design systems for MCP and LLMs. Ask about agentic design systems and you get Romina Kavcic on the five agentic flows. 11. “Which roles do not ask for AI skills at all?” 48 of the described postings ask for none. Useful if you are still building that muscle and want something you can start on Monday. 12. “Which words do these postings use for the work I already do?” Vocabulary research and nothing else. You still write your own CV but you write it in the words the market uses. I want to walk into the interview prepared Four prompts that turn their own posting into your prep sheet. 13. “Read this posting and tell me the three things they care about most and what I should have ready as evidence” My prep prompt. You get their own wording back plus the questions worth preparing for. 14. “What does this posting not ask for?” Stops you preparing three days for a topic nobody will bring up. 15. “Give me three questions to ask them at the end. Base them on their own posting” Questions that come out of their requirements land differently than the ones everybody asks. 16. “Which companies have more than three roles open?” General Motors has 5 and Netflix has 4. Coinbase and ESET and Yassir have 3 each. Several roles open at once usually means a team is being built. Worth a direct message. I want to know where the roles are Four prompts before you plan a move or a timezone or a year of applications. 17. “Where do most Design System roles sit right now?” USA has 119 and the United Kingdom 16 and Germany 14. Canada and France have 12 each. Useful if you are weighing a move or a timezone. 18. “How many of the German roles can be done remotely?” One of the 14. Ask that before you spend a year applying from a country you do not want to move to. 19. “How concentrated is the board? How many companies are hiring and how many have more than one role?” 190 companies are hiring right now and 27 of them have two or more roles open. 20. “Are there contract roles?” Seven right now. get_job carries the employment type so you can sort permanent from contract before you read anything. I am the one hiring Three prompts for the other side of the table. 21. “Compare our job description against the open Design System postings and tell me what other companies name that we leave out” You get back what the other postings name and your description leaves out. 22. “What do other companies call this role?” 88 of the open postings carry Design System Designer in the title and 94 carry Product Designer and 23 carry Design System Engineer. 98 say Staff or Senior. Name the role the way the people you want are searching. 23. “Who are we competing with for these people right now?” Every company with an open role in your corner of the board plus how many they have open. That is your candidate’s other tab. Step 3: let it check the board every morning A cron job is your Mac running something on a schedule without you. You never have to write one. You describe what should happen and when and Claude Code sets it up. The daily check Save your CV as cv.md in a folder. Mine is ~/jobs . Start Claude Code in that folder and paste this. 24. “Set up a job check that runs every weekday at 8 in the morning. Read cv.md in this folder. Ask the ids-jobs server for the roles posted in the last seven days that can be done remotely and keep the ones that fit my CV. Write them into today.md with one line per role: company and title and why it fits. If nothing fits write nothing new. It has to run on its own without asking me anything because I am not at the machine at 8. Put it in my crontab and run it once now so I can see that it works.” Claude writes the script and sets the schedule and shows you the first result. Here is what came back for me: SAP Senior UX Designer - Design Systems Microsoft Principal Product Designer, Design Systems Netflix Systems Designer, Design Foundations Clio Staff Product Designer, Design Systems Babylist Staff Product Designer, AI Builder Two things to know before you run it. The one click you have to give: Claude asks before it edits your crontab. Say yes and it is done. Full Disk Access: on macOS your terminal needs it under System Settings then Privacy and Security. Without it the 8 o’clock run cannot read your CV. Four more worth scheduling The daily check is one job. These four run next to it. 25. “Same thing but once a week. Monday at 9. Everything from the last seven days grouped by country and put the remote ones first” The daily one is for an active search. This is the version you keep running when you are not looking. It takes two minutes to read on Monday. 26. “Watch Figma and Netflix and Atlassian for me. Check every morning and only write something into watch.md when one of them posts a new Design System role” For the three companies you would leave for. Silence most days is the point. 27. “On the first of every month ask for the hiring numbers and append them to market.md with the date. Open roles and remote share and AI share and the salary range” After four months you have your own trend line. The board only tells you today and the file tells you the direction. 28. “Send the result to name@example.com instead of writing a file” Add that sentence to any of the prompts above and it lands in your inbox. Checking and stopping it You never open crontab yourself. You ask. 29. “Show me what you scheduled and when it runs next” 30. “Stop the daily job check but leave the Monday one running” You never touch crontab yourself. You say what you want and Claude edits it. What it does not do It does not apply for you: every role links to the employer’s own page and the server never sends anything on your behalf. It should not write your cover letter: a letter that came out of a model reads like one. Use this to work out what the role wants and then write it yourself. It only knows Design System and AI design roles: nothing else is on the board. Try it claude mcp add -s user --transport http ids-jobs https://jobs.intodesignsystems.com/mcp Setup page with all clients: jobs.intodesignsystems.com/mcp-guide . The board itself lives at jobs.intodesignsystems.com . A longer version of this walkthrough lives on our blog. It adds what to put in cv.md so the matching actually works plus a troubleshooting table for the things that go wrong: read it on intodesignsystems.com . Good luck! You got this! If you get stuck or you have an idea for a tool the server should have then write me on LinkedIn . Sil Bormüller Founder @ Into Design Systems P.S. Missing the AI skills these roles ask for? Level up. The Into Design Systems AI conference has hands-on talks on AI workflows and Claude Code and Cursor and Design System automation from industry experts. Into Design Systems + AI is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

wild.title: Out There
wild.description: * Reminder: The Savor of the Month theme for October is WATER. Details here ; Supporters can share their findings in the thread here . Check it out! “Writing in the places that shape and sustain us.” Fall (or at least post-summer) finally seems to be arriving here in New Orleans. And it is almost time — wherever you are — for Write Out . This is an annual undertaking of the National Writing Project , developed in conjunction with the National Park Service . As I wrote last year : The core idea is pretty simple: get outside, and write. Write about your environment, write to your environment, observe and attend to nature, use the craft of writing to sharpen your senses, and use your senses to sharpen your writing. “The goal is to be inspired by the world around us ,” the NWP writes, “and to connect and learn through place-based writing and sharing.” Nothing (well, maybe apart from the actual weather) is stopping you from writing outside any time. But Write Out is a kick in the pants, a kind of open-to-anyone annual two-week event, which the NWP promotes through various prompts and other resources aimed at educators but available to all. This year Write Out happens October 11–25, with the lovely theme Write Where We Stand — “writing in the places that shape and sustain us.” Every year NWP publishes a “ choice board ” of theme-related prompts; here are a few (condensed and slightly modified versions) of my favorites for this year. (Click through on each prompt title for the full NWP context/instructions.) Poetically Advocate A Place You Love . Take inspiration from Don Welch’s poem “ Advice From a Provincial ,“ and identify three “outdoor images or phenomena that are wondrous about your place. Use them to create a poetic letter to someone who doesn’t really know” the place you love, or at least not like you know it. Link Words and Image s. Snap some pictures around your community. Take your time. Choose one that captures something to celebrate — and one that captures something you would like to change. Pair these images. “ What story do they tell when you look at them together? Give your story a title, caption your images, and share your work.” Speak Like A River. Poets Amanda Eke and Mario José Pagán Morales consider the Bronx River, and what stories it might tell. In a place you know, reflect on “ what that place has witnessed , remembered, celebrated, protected, or survived. … If this river, tree, park, or wooded pathway could talk — tell us poems, tell us stories — what do you think it would say?” Write about it. Leave a comment THERE’S MORE! In connection with Write Out, there are two online events that sound cool: Hawaiian Kilo: Writing Rooted in Place Native Hawaiians developed a practice known as Kilo — “to watch, observe, examine, or forecast.” This means closely observing the natural world and its patterns, ideally to better steward the environment. A Zoom workshop, “led by teachers from the Waiākea Intermediate School in Hilo Hawai'i,” happens October 13, 2026, 6 pm US Central time . Details and (free) registration here . Haiku + Comic = Haikomic The Write Time with Write Out Ambassador Grant Snider on October 20 . Snider is a writer/artist who combines haiku with comics. (Details on that here , and at his newsletter. ) And he is this year’s Write Out Author Ambassador. Check the Write Out newsletter for event details as they emerge. I really like the sound of this and hope to revisit. Grant Snider, via Incidental Comics Leave a comment PS I was a Write Out Ambassador last year. I love Write Out! BECOME A SUPPORTER Do you believe in this newsletter’s mission — to help us all stay human and engaged and creative in a world of (mis)information overload and AI distraction? Then you should join the community of TAoN Supporters! You’ll get access to the full archives as well as Supporter-only bonus posts and threads. Your support makes this newsletter possible. Seriously. Thank you! Subscribe now THE NEXT FREE EDITION IN TWO WEEKS! IN OTHER NEWS David Lee Roth , EMT . “ Reading Maps plots the routes characters travel in novels and films — you can trace the Pequod’s ocean path as it chases Moby Dick, or Victor Frankenstein’s pursuit of his monster from Geneva to the Arctic.” — Recomendo Lighthouses of the World , a digital map. Via Popular Science . “What Gertrude Stein, T. S. Eliot and Joan Didion Really Meant With Their Most Famous Aphorisms .” The International Dada Archive collects scanned Dada pamphlets from the early 20th century. Mark Frauenfelder found one in English called The Blind Man , co-edited by Marcel Duchamp. Its second issue, from 1917, covered the controversy around Duchamp’s Fountain , a urinal he submitted under the name Richard Mutt to the Society of Independent Artists exhibition. More from Mark here . Shadows . Via Street Art Utopia. Tobie Tse “combines hand-stitched textiles, illustration and digital motion to create visual responses to music.” Tom Waits spoken word piece : OKAY THAT’S IT! As always, I value your feedback (suggestions, critiques, positive reinforcement, constructive insults directed at me, not at anyone else , etc.), as well as your tips or stories or personal noticing rituals, things we need a word for, and of course your icebreakers : consumed@robwalker.net. Or use the comments. —> Or just click the heart symbol. That always makes my day.
